rules.statement: When authenticating a client by a JWT `client_assertion`, require `iss` and `sub` to be present and equal, use the unverified `sub` only to look up the client's registered keys, and trust no other claim until the signature verifies against those keys.
rules.why: OpenID Connect Core §9 requires iss == sub == client_id, and the unverified payload must not be trusted beyond locating the verification keys.
rules.check: Look for client-assertion code that reads claims other than `sub` before signature verification, skips the iss/sub equality check, or accepts a missing iss or sub.

rules.statement: Identify the client of a JWT-bearer client authentication from the assertion's `sub`, and don't require a separate `client_id` form parameter.
rules.why: FAPI `private_key_jwt` clients send only the assertion, and §9 already pins sub to the client_id.
rules.check: Look for JWT-bearer client authentication that rejects requests without a `client_id` parameter or that resolves the client from `client_id` instead of the assertion.

rules.statement: Accept a client assertion's `aud` when it equals either the issuer identifier or the URL of the endpoint receiving it, and reject any other audience.
rules.why: FAPI 2.0 §5.3.2.1 requires the issuer and OIDC Core §9 permits the token endpoint URL, so accepting both lets standard and FAPI clients interoperate.
rules.check: Look for audience validation of client assertions that accepts only one of the two values, accepts arbitrary audiences, or skips the check.

rules.statement: Require `exp` on client assertions, and reject replay by recording each `jti` as single-use in shared expiring state, written atomically and keyed by tenant, client_id and jti.
rules.why: RFC 7523 §3 requires single-use assertions. A non-atomic or per-instance record lets the same assertion be replayed across concurrent requests or replicas.
rules.check: Look for client-assertion validation that accepts a missing `exp` or `jti`, does a separate check and then a write instead of an atomic add-if-absent, keys replay entries without the tenant or client, or keeps them only in process memory.

rules.statement: For `private_key_jwt`, reject assertions whose `alg` is `none`, symmetric (HMAC) or unknown. For `client_secret_jwt`, accept only HMAC algorithms. Classify the algorithm by its registered key type rather than by matching strings.
rules.why: Each method must only accept its own key family, so that asymmetric authentication can't be downgraded to a shared secret or to an unsigned token.
rules.check: Look for assertion validation that lets `alg=none` or an unrecognized alg through, lets an HMAC alg satisfy `private_key_jwt`, or decides the key family by checking alg name prefixes.

rules.statement: When `token_endpoint_auth_signing_alg_values_supported` is configured, reject client assertions whose `alg` is not in that list.
rules.why: The algorithms advertised in discovery must match the algorithms actually accepted.
rules.check: Look for client-assertion validation that ignores the configured supported signing algorithm list.

rules.statement: Implement each client authentication method as its own handler that advertises exactly one method and defers on requests it doesn't own, and derive `token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported` from the registered handlers instead of a hand-maintained list.
rules.why: Deriving discovery from the handlers keeps the advertised methods truthful, and each request gets handled exactly once.
rules.check: Look for a single handler that claims more than one auth method, discovery metadata that lists auth methods by hand, or a handler that returns an error for a request belonging to a sibling handler's method.

rules.statement: Don't let `client_secret_jwt` or other symmetric client authentication satisfy a FAPI profile; FAPI deployments must require `private_key_jwt` or mutual TLS.
rules.why: The FAPI security profiles require strong (asymmetric or mTLS) client authentication and exclude symmetric methods.
rules.check: Look for FAPI profile configuration or checks that list `client_secret_jwt`, `client_secret_basic` or `client_secret_post` as allowed.
